guidance: A planning estimate, not a measurement: it assumes steady traffic, one data record per expired flow and independent per-packet sampling. Templates, option records and retransmissions are excluded, and real exporters expire entries differently, so compare the result with the exporter counters before sizing a collector.
method: Packet rate is throughput in Mbit/s times one million, divided by eight times the average packet size in bytes. New flows per second are that packet rate divided by the average number of packets per flow. A sampling interval of N selects one packet in N independently, as systematic packet sampling is modelled in RFC 5476, so a flow of k packets reaches the collector with probability 1 - (1 - 1/N)^k; the observed flow rate is the true flow rate times that probability, and N of 1 gives a probability of exactly 1. RFC 7011 defines the IPFIX data record, so the estimate exports one data record per observed flow when it expires, which in steady state equals the rate at which observed flows enter the cache. Export bit rate is records per second times record size times eight; daily volume is records per second times record size times 86400; retained volume is daily volume times retention divided by one billion for decimal gigabytes. The cache figure is the observed flow rate times the active timeout, the upper bound on entries an exporter holds when an inactive timeout flushes idle flows sooner. Templates, option records, transport overhead and retransmissions are not counted. Results round the packet rate to whole packets, flow rates to two decimals, observed flows and records to three, the bit rate and daily bytes to whole units, retained volume to three decimals, the cache to whole entries and coverage to two decimals. Throughput is limited to 400,000 Mbit/s, packet size to 64-9000 bytes, packets per flow to 1-1,000,000, the sampling interval to a whole number from 1 to 1,000,000, the timeout to 1-3600 seconds, the record size to 16-1500 bytes and retention to 1-3650 days.
